official.deadline_note: Brown's published financial aid filing deadlines: Early Decision applicants - CSS Profile and FAFSA both due November 2, 2026; Regular Decision applicants - CSS Profile and FAFSA both due February 1, 2027. Aid must be applied for at the time of the admission application.
official.application_cycle: 2026-27 admission cycle for fall 2027 entry (CSS Profile available to complete online as of October 1, 2026)
official.status_note: The CSS Profile is available to complete online as of October 1, 2026 for the current cycle; filing deadlines are November 2, 2026 (Early Decision) and February 1, 2027 (Regular Decision).
official.tuition_coverage_note: In most cases, financial aid awards are applied directly to the student account as a credit towards the cost of tuition, fees, room and meals. The financial aid award will help with the cost of travel, books and personal expenses, but it does not assist with vacation and summer expenses.
official.funding_period: per year (average; actual award set by demonstrated need)

Brown meets 100% of each student's demonstrated financial need

eligibility: International students are eligible to apply for University financial aid

requirements: Indicate on the admission application that you are applying for financial aid
Submit the CSS Profile (CSS code 3189) by the applicable deadline; required from each parent if parents are divorced or separated
Submit the FAFSA by the applicable deadline if a U.S. citizen or permanent resident

English language proficiency must be achieved before international students are admitted

FAFSA (for U.S. citizens and permanent residents)

Official English proficiency test score reports for matriculating students who self-report a result
selection_criteria: All Brown financial aid is need-based; the University does not offer merit awards
Aid is awarded based on demonstrated financial need determined from the CSS Profile (and FAFSA where applicable)
A provisional financial aid decision is included with the admission decision when all required aid materials are submitted by the deadline
Brown continues to consider transfer students' financial need when making admission decisions
coverage: Travel (the award helps with the cost of travel)
Personal expenses (the award helps with the cost of personal expenses)
Not covered: vacation and summer expenses
application_method: Apply for admission to Brown and indicate that you are applying for financial aid
Submit the CSS Profile at cssprofile.collegeboard.org (CSS code 3189) by the Early Decision or Regular Decision aid deadline
Submit the FAFSA if you are a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
Respond to College Board IDOC requests for tax or other income documentation after filing the CSS Profile
official.application_route: Apply for admission to Brown indicating that you seek financial aid, then file the CSS Profile (FAFSA as well for U.S. citizens/permanent residents) by the Early Decision or Regular Decision aid deadline; Brown issues a provisional award with the admission decision.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction for seeking aid: international students are eligible to apply for University financial aid. The FAFSA is intended for U.S. citizens and permanent residents.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible to apply for University financial aid, and Brown is need-blind for international students beginning with the Class of 2029.
official.description: Brown University provides entirely need-based institutional financial aid to international undergraduate applicants: international students who apply for aid at the time they apply for admission have their full demonstrated need met, with no packaged loans under The Brown Promise, and Brown is need-blind for international students beginning with the Class of 2029.
official.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid for international applicants
official.english_requirement: Minimum scores expected in most cases: TOEFL internet-based exam taken prior to January 2026 - 105; TOEFL internet-based exam taken January 2026 and later - 5.5; IELTS - 8.0; Duolingo Test of English - 130; Pearson Test of English - 75; C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency Cambridge English exams - 191. Testing is highly recommended for applicants for whom English is not a first language, the primary language spoken at home, or the language of instruction; official score reports are required for all matriculating students who self-report a result.

applicant_utility.summary: Brown's aid for international undergraduates is entirely need-based: tick the financial-aid box on your admission application and file the CSS Profile by the deadline, and if admitted you are awarded up to your full demonstrated need in scholarships with no packaged loans under The Brown Promise. From the Class of 2029 onward, requesting aid no longer counts against international applicants in admission. The average need-based scholarship for the Class of 2029 was $64,274 against a published 2025-26 cost of attendance of $97,284, so most aided students still cover a contribution (student work or a small student contribution) themselves.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International applicants from families who cannot cover the roughly $97,000 annual cost and who can document family finances in detail early in the application season.
application_readiness_checklist: Tick the financial-aid box on the Brown admission application itself before submitting - aid cannot be added later
Start the CSS Profile as soon as it opens on October 1 and submit well ahead of the ED (Nov 2, 2026) or RD (Feb 1, 2027) deadline
Gather 2025 tax documents or non-tax filer statements for both parents; divorced or separated parents each file their own CSS Profile
If your country does not issue tax returns, obtain an employer statement of 2024 annual earnings in advance
Monitor email for College Board IDOC requests and upload documents promptly
common_rejection_risks: Failing to request aid on the admission application, which removes eligibility for Brown's need-based institutional aid entirely
Filing the CSS Profile after the deadline - a provisional award is only issued when materials arrive on time
Substituting the ISFAA form or a paper CSS Profile, which the Office of Financial Aid does not accept
Only one parent completing the CSS Profile when parents are divorced or separated
Applicants from Iran or North Korea discovering too late that they cannot use the CSS Profile and missing the email-first alternative
Leaving IDOC document requests unanswered until after the admission decision
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Vacation and summer expenses are explicitly not covered by the award. Aid helps with travel, books and personal expenses but publishes no fixed amounts for them, so budget for visa fees, flights beyond what the award helps with, and summer living costs; the published 2025-26 cost of attendance is $97,284 per year.
document_audit: CSS Profile must be filed electronically through College Board with code 3189; Brown offers no fee waivers and rejects ISFAA or paper submissions
Each divorced or separated parent must submit their own CSS Profile
IDOC requests specifically call for 2025 tax documents - paperwork for the wrong tax year stalls the award
Employer earnings statements for 2024 substitute for tax returns only where no tax return is filed in the student's country
Self-reported English scores must be verified by official reports sent before they expire and no later than May 2027 for fall 2027 entry; MyBest combined scores are not accepted
alerts: Aid must be requested with the admission application itself; there is no later add-on route for entering students
Deferral does not upgrade your aid policy: eligibility follows the class you first applied to, and need-aware entrants who did not apply for aid cannot apply in later years
If your English test score expires before May 2027 you must retake the same exam before matriculation
Brown warns that U.S. immigration rules and restrictions on off-campus summer work make it essential to know exactly where vacation and summer funds will come from
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One integrated online process: admission application with the aid box ticked, CSS Profile through College Board, FAFSA only for U.S. citizens/permanent residents, then IDOC document collection and a provisional award released alongside the admission decision.
